html:
The Treaty of Trianon was the peace treaty signed at the Trianon palace at Versailles on 4 June 1920 between the Allies and Hungary after World War I, which took about two thirds of the old Kingdom of Hungary's land.

Slovakia and Ruthenia went to Czechoslovakia, Transylvania to Romania, Croatia and the south to the new Yugoslav state, and a strip to Austria. Hungary lost more than half its people, and about three million Hungarians found themselves outside the new borders. Most lost land had non Hungarian majorities, but the cuts also took whole Hungarian regions. Grief over Trianon drove interwar Hungarian politics and its alliance with Nazi Germany, which briefly returned some land. 4 June is a day of national remembrance, and the treaty still shapes ties with neighbours.
sum: The Treaty of Trianon was the peace treaty signed at the Trianon palace at Versailles on 4 June 1920 between the Allies and Hungary after World War I, which took about two thirds of the old Kingdom of Hungary's land.
